To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EMIM/Ferroelectrics junctions can be utilized to develop new types of nonvolatile memory devices with high density and fast speed.

an Edge Metal- Insulator-Metal (MIM) junction of crossbar structure can show an enormous change of tunneling resistance by the modulation of the electric fringe field associated with the polarization of an underlying ferrelectric layer, and the single three-terminal EMiM/ferroelectric structure could form a memory cell without any selection devices.
the EMIM/Ferroelectrics structures are promising candidates for the next generation of non-volatile memories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electrical characteristics of the edge metal-insulator-metal (EMIM) ferroelectric tunnel junctions.
the development of novel ferroelectric memory devices based on ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs).
the design, fabrication and characterization of ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) and ferroelectric memory devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ferroelectric fringe field induced resistance change in an EMIM junction is a promising mechanism to realize a new type of non-volatile resistance change memory devices with high density, low power, and low cost.
the ferroelectric fringe field induced EMIM tunnel resistance modulation is a new and promising mechanism for the development of next generation non-volatile memory technology.

this work demonstrates a new approach of using ferroelectric fringe field to induce giant electroresistance in EMIM junctions, which can be used to develop a new type of all-thin-films-based, non-volatile, ferroelectric memory devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ferroelectric field effect transistor (FeFET) can be used as a memory device, which has the potential of being integrated with CMOS devices to form a new type of 3D non-volatile memory.

a huge change in tunnel resistance of an EMIM/Ferroeletric structure can be induced via the modulation of electric field fringe effect, associated with polarization switching of the ferroelectric layer, which could form a non-volatile memory cell without any selection device.
the ferroelectricity in a thin layer is able to induce a large change in the tunnel resistance of a neighboring metal-insulator-metal junction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EMIM junctions could provide a new type of memory device with the potential to be used in future 3D memory architectures, which is highly desirable in terms of high density, high performance, and low cost.
the fringe field of a ferroelectric layer can induce a huge change of resistance in an EMIM junction.
a ferroelectric fringe field can be used to induce a giant electroresistance effect in an EMIM structure.
